# Facilitator Guide — AI Content Governance & Brand Safety

Slides: `slides/slides.md`. Demos: `demos/`. Exercise sheets: `exercises.md`. Every demo runs offline; start times assume 09:30.

**One week before:** run `python demos/run_all.py`. Confirm room, projector, one laptop per pair, Wi-Fi. Print exercises and handouts.

## Day 1

| Time | Segment | What you do and say |
|---|---|---|
| 09:30 | Welcome | Outcomes on the first slide. Ask each table for the one question they want answered; write them on the flipchart. |
| 09:40 | **Module 1 — Rules for generated content** | Teach: disclosure, watermarking / provenance, IP and licensing, regulated claims. |
| 10:01 | Demo 1 | **Run `python demos/01_content_policy_check.py`** — a content policy as data applied to five assets: disclosure, provenance record, IP/licence and regulated claims — with the rule that failed. Close with: *“A content policy nobody can test is a poster. Write it as rules you can run against an asset.”* |
| 10:16 | Lab 1 | Policy draft — see `exercises.md`. Walk the room; collect one result per table. |
| 10:40 | **Module 2 — Brand risk** | Teach: deepfakes, impersonation, monitoring, response plan. |
| 11:01 | Break |  |
| 11:16 | Demo 2 | **Run `python demos/02_impersonation_response.py`** — an impersonation incident triaged by reach and harm into a timed response plan with owners, and the monitoring signals that would have caught it earlier. Close with: *“You cannot stop someone cloning your CEO. You can decide today who does what in the first hour.”* |
| 11:31 | Lab 2 | Response playbook — see `exercises.md`. Walk the room; collect one result per table. |
| 11:55 | Close | Assessment: Content governance policy. Return to the flipchart questions — tick the ones answered. |

## If short on time

Keep every demo; shorten the teaching before it. Cut labs to a paired discussion of the lab question rather than dropping them. Never cut the close.

## What can go wrong

- **A demo fails on the day** — you ran `run_all.py` last week, so it is the environment: `pip install -r requirements.txt`, then re-run. Screenshots of each output live in nobody's folder: take them after your dry run.
- **No projector / terminal too small** — open `/demos` in a browser and run the same demo from the *Course labs* section.
- **The room has no laptops** — run labs as table discussions using the printed exercise sheet; you run the script and change the inputs they call out.
